.title: Market structure *complete*
.yt_title: Market Structure Fully Explained – HH/HL, BOS, CHoCH & Multi-Timeframe (H4 → M5) on Gold
.chapters[0].title: Market structure complete
.chapters[0].segs[0].say: If you don't know which way the market is moving, every entry is a coin flip. That's why market structure is the foundation of everything we do on the gold chart.
.chapters[0].segs[1].say: In this video we'll go through it completely: highs and lows in a trend, the break of structure, the change of character – and how to connect several timeframes, from the four-hour to the five-minute chart.
.chapters[0].segs[2].say: Important up front: this is educational content, not investment advice. Trading involves risk of loss. Practise new strategies on a demo account first.
.chapters[1].title: The *uptrend*
.chapters[1].hook: How to read an uptrend correctly
.chapters[1].segs[0].say: Let's start with the uptrend. A trend isn't an opinion – it's a sequence of highs and lows that you can clearly read on the chart.
.chapters[1].segs[1].say: The market rises and forms a high. If it's exceeded later, we call it a higher high, or H H.
.chapters[1].segs[2].say: Then comes a pullback. What matters is where it ends: if the new low stays above the previous one, it's a higher low, or H L.
.chapters[1].segs[3].say: Now you mark the last high. This line shows you where the trend has to prove it's continuing.
.chapters[1].segs[4].say: If a candle closes above this line, we have a break of structure to the upside. The trend is confirmed.
.chapters[1].segs[5].say: And it continues like this: a new higher low, a new break of structure. As long as this chain holds, you only look for trade ideas on the buy side.
.chapters[2].title: The *downtrend*
.chapters[2].segs[0].say: The downtrend works exactly the other way round. Here you look for lower lows and lower highs.
.chapters[2].segs[1].say: The market falls and forms a low. If it's undercut, it's a lower low, or L L.
.chapters[2].segs[2].say: The recovery afterwards stays below the previous high. That's a lower high, or L H. The buyers no longer manage to make new highs.
.chapters[2].segs[3].say: The last low is now the line you watch.
.chapters[2].segs[4].say: If a candle closes below it, that's a break of structure to the downside. The downtrend continues.
.chapters[2].segs[5].say: Here too the pattern repeats. As long as lower highs and lower lows form, only sells are an option for you.
.chapters[3].title: Wick or *close*?
.chapters[3].segs[0].say: Now comes a point where many traders fail: the question of when a high is really broken.
.chapters[3].segs[1].say: We have an uptrend with a clear high.
.chapters[3].segs[2].say: After the pullback a higher low forms. The line at the last high is drawn.
.chapters[3].segs[3].say: Then a wick pokes above the high – but the candle closes back below it. Anyone who buys here often walks straight into a trap.
.chapters[3].segs[4].say: Price falls back. That wasn't a break of structure – more of a grab for the liquidity above the high.
.chapters[3].segs[5].say: Only this candle closes clearly above the high. Now the break of structure is confirmed.
.chapters[3].segs[6].say: The rule is simple: the closing price counts, not the wick. That protects you from many premature entries.
.chapters[4].title: Remember *this*
.chapters[4].segs[1].say: A wick above the high doesn't count as a break.
.chapters[4].segs[2].say: Only the candle close confirms it.
.chapters[5].title: Change of *Character*
.chapters[5].hook: How to spot a trend reversal early
.chapters[5].segs[0].say: No trend runs forever. The change of character is the first hint that the structure is turning.
.chapters[5].segs[1].say: Here we see a downtrend with lower highs and lower lows.
.chapters[5].segs[2].say: You mark the last lower high. It's the line the sellers have to defend.
.chapters[5].segs[3].say: The market makes one more lower low, but the sell-off is losing strength.
.chapters[5].segs[4].say: Then a candle closes above the last lower high. That's the change of character. The downtrend is broken – but the new trend isn't confirmed yet.
.chapters[5].segs[5].say: The reversal is only confirmed by a higher low and a break of structure to the upside. In short: the CHoCH warns, the BOS confirms.
.chapters[6].title: From *H4* to *M5*
.chapters[6].hook: H4 for direction, M5 for the entry
.chapters[6].segs[0].say: Finally, we connect the timeframes. The bigger chart sets the direction, the smaller one gives you the precise entry.
.chapters[6].segs[1].say: On the four-hour chart there's an uptrend, and price is coming into a zone it previously rallied from. On the five-minute chart we still see a correction to the downside.
.chapters[6].segs[2].say: In the zone, a wick takes the stops below the last low. That's a sweep.
.chapters[6].segs[3].say: Then the five-minute chart closes above the last lower high. The change of character shows: the small structure is turning in the direction of the big trend.
.chapters[6].segs[4].say: The entry comes on the pullback, with the stop below the sweep low. That keeps the risk small and clearly defined.
.chapters[6].segs[5].say: If the plan works out, price runs toward the next high. But even the best setup can fail – that's why the stop always belongs in the trade.
.chapters[7].title: The *summary*
.chapters[7].segs[1].say: Higher highs and higher lows mean an uptrend, lower highs and lower lows mean a downtrend.
.chapters[7].segs[2].say: A break of structure confirms the trend – but only with a candle close, not with a wick.
.chapters[7].segs[2].bullet: BOS only with a candle close
.chapters[7].segs[3].say: The change of character is a warning. The reversal is only confirmed with a higher low and a new break of structure.
.chapters[7].segs[4].say: The direction comes from the four-hour chart, the entry from the five-minute chart.
.chapters[7].segs[5].say: And no matter how clear the structure looks: risk only a small part of your account per trade, about one to two percent.
.chapters[8].segs[0].say: If you want to practise market structure with us on the gold chart every day: join our free gold group on Telegram. You'll find the link in the description.
